A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the basal cells of the airway pseudostratified columnar epithelium are a heterogeneous cell population that includes a small population of stem cells that are multipotent and self-renewing.

we have identified a population of cells that are capable of self-renewal and differentiation into all of the cell types found in the pseudostratification of the airway, including ciliated cells and secretory cells.
the airway basal cells are the most important cell type for understanding the pathophysiology and treatment of airway diseases, such as COPD and asthma.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the airway epithelial basal cell population, and the stem cell niche in which it resides, is a key regulator of epithelial differentiation and remodeling, and that it may be a therapeutic target in airway diseases.
basal cells are not simply a ‘reserve cell’ population of the airway.
basal cells are the primary cell type that is responsible for airway epithelial repair.
